chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Bunān ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
If a man eats from the sacrificial offering voluntarily given, then there is nothing upon him; but if it was obligatory, then the value of what he ate is upon him.

key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering presented in hajj
key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: as a voluntary act, not legally required
key_terms.قِيمَةُ: the monetary value or compensation due
key_terms.مَا أَكَلَ: what he consumed from the offering

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat from an obligatory sacrificial offering in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning eating from sacrificial offerings in hajj. It distinguishes between a voluntary offering, from which eating carries no liability, and an obligatory offering, from which eating requires compensation equal to the value of what was eaten.
